title: Python Foundations
summary: Everyone starts here. From your first print() to programs that ask, decide, repeat, remember and save: variables, input, decisions, loops, lists and dictionaries, functions and files. Real Python runs in your browser.
prereq: Nothing: no coding or maths background is needed. About 14 and up, or 12–13 with a teacher.
outcomes: Write and run Python programs that print, calculate and ask questions.
Store values in variables and build messages with f-strings.
Make decisions with if, elif, else, and/or/not and match-case.
Repeat work with while and for loops, and keep data in lists and dictionaries.
Write functions that take values in and give results back, and read Python’s error messages.
Tidy text, save data to files, and build Pocket Bank, an expense tracker.

levels.name: Beginner
levels.who: First contact with code, or a non-tech learner who needs the useful core.
levels.outcome: Write small programs that ask, decide, repeat and save, with the lessons to lean on. Pocket Bank: add, list and total.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.who: Most learners, and what PY2 and most streams expect.
levels.outcome: Read errors, handle messy input, and build Pocket Bank with categories, monthly totals and saving to a file.

levelNote: PY1 stops at Intermediate because its depth continues in PY2 · Intermediate Python.

project.title: Pocket Bank: an expense tracker that saves to a file
project.brief: Beginner: add, list and total expenses. Intermediate: categories, monthly totals and saving to a file. One brief, a checklist per level, hidden tests and three “explain your code” questions.
